name: Jason Marsh
summary: Director of Technology with 13+ years across IT, assistive technology services, and team leadership. Designs, ships, and operates production software by directing AI coding agents (Claude Code) - owning the product decisions, specification, testing, deployment, and users - including WhatCanHelp, a free assistive-technology discovery site covering thousands of products. Restructured AT billing at a nonprofit, growing annual service revenue from $17K to over $200K within a year. ATACP-certified in assistive technology assessment. Sets the organization's guidance on safe staff use of AI.

projects.name: WhatCanHelp
projects.desc: (whatcanhelp.com) - free assistive-technology discovery site for families, clients, and AT professionals who otherwise search vendor catalogs one at a time. Specified and shipped a freeform needs intake that returns a matched shortlist, complexity ratings so users know what setup a device needs, state-by-state borrowing and funding directories, and PDF reports for funding meetings and IEP appendices. Chose batch AI classification with prompt caching to keep a catalog of thousands of products affordable to maintain, with schema checks against fabricated product data. Built with AI coding agents; Node/Express + SQLite, self-hosted. Operated in production.

projects.name: MCP Servers
projects.desc: - custom Model Context Protocol servers connecting Claude agents to self-hosted apps and everyday tools, with guardrails: hooks, sandboxing, approval gates on actions with side effects, and prompt-injection containment. Built with AI coding agents; in daily use.

projects.name: MealDeck
projects.desc: - meal-planning app for friends and family: grocery lists grouped by shared ingredients, hands-free voice cook mode, and AI recipe adaptation for dietary needs and serving sizes. Ran as a private beta.

projects.name: RadioGridXL
projects.desc: - internet radio for older adults and people with disabilities: large buttons, no accounts or ads, screen-reader support, WCAG AA contrast. Designed a technician-only settings panel so staff can configure a device without exposing that complexity to the listener. Deployed at my organization and piloted with older adults.

projects.name: PetFeedr
projects.desc: - Raspberry Pi pet feeder built because the store-bought one tipped over and ran out of food; web interface for schedules and portions, feed-time randomization, one-command deploy. Running daily for about two years.

projects.name: EchoEtcher
projects.desc: - turns voice memos recorded while driving into tagged, structured notes in Obsidian; local Whisper transcription and a local LLM (Ollama) keep recordings on the machine by default. In personal use; being reworked.

projects.name: InfoVault (in development)
projects.desc: - handheld device for people with vision loss that uses a camera and an LLM to read text aloud and describe objects; prototype in development.
